Rashi on Nazir 30a:1:1.hebrew: אלא - אליבא דרבי, כגון דאמר: אהא בשביל אבא, אהא בשביל עצמי:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:1:1.english: Rather - According to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi, it is a case] such as where he said: "I shall be [a nazirite] on account of Father; I shall be [a nazirite] on account of myself."

Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:1.hebrew: אי אייתי ב' שערות מעיקרא - כלומר, הניחא דמתרצת מתני' כוותיה דרבי, דלא מיחייב אלא בחדא נזירות, אילו אייתי ב' שערות מקמי הזירו אבוה:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:1.english: If he had developed two hairs from the outset - That is to say, it works out well that you explain the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], that he is obligated in only one naziriteship if he had developed two hairs before his father made him a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:2.hebrew: קאים בנזירות דידיה - כדקאמר איהו: אם אני גדול, שהבאתי שתי שערות, שאיני נתפס בשל אבא — אהא בשביל עצמי. ואי אייתי שתי שערות לבסוף דהדירו אביו — קאי בנזירות דאבוה, ולא חייל עליה נזירות דידיה כלל; דהא לא קביל עליה נזירות אלא אם אינו נתפס בשביל אביו, וכיון דעדיין לא הביא ב' שערות — חל עליה נזירות דאבוה, ולא חייל עליה נזירות דידיה כלל:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:2.english: He stands bound by his own naziriteship - As he [the son] said: "If I am an adult, having developed two [pubic] hairs, such that I am not bound by [the vow of my] father, let me be [a nazirite] on my own behalf." And if he developed two hairs subsequently, after his father had vowed for him, he stands [bound] by the naziriteship of his father, and his own naziriteship does not take effect upon him at all; for he did not accept naziriteship upon himself except if he is not bound on account of his father, and since he had not yet developed two hairs, the naziriteship of his father took effect upon him, and his own naziriteship did not take effect upon him at all.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:3.hebrew: ואי אייתי באמצע - לא ידעינן אי בההיא שעתא דהדירו אביו אייתי ב' שערות אי לא. מי ניחא? והא כיון דאמר אהא בשביל אבא, אהא בשביל עצמי אם אינו נתפס בשביל אביו, ואפשר דקאים בשתים עשרה והגיע לעונת נדרים ועדיין לא הביא ב' שערות, וחל עליו נזירות שלו ונזירות של אביו — כיצד אתה פוטרו בנזירות אחת? והא מיחייב למיקם בנזירות על שלו ועל של אביו:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:2:3.english: And if he developed [two hairs] in the middle - [Meaning,] we do not know whether at that time when his father declared him a nazirite he had developed two hairs or not. Does this work out well? Behold, since he said: “I shall be [a nazirite] on account of [my] father, [and] I shall be [a nazirite] on account of myself if I am not bound on account of [my] father,” and it is possible that he is twelve [years old] and has reached the age of vows and has not yet developed two hairs, and [both] his own naziriteship and his father's naziriteship take effect upon him — how can you exempt him with one naziriteship? Behold, he is obligated to observe naziriteship for his own [vow] and for his father's [vow]!

Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג: הניחא לרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה דאמר עד שיגיע לעונת נדרים, אלא לרבי דאמר עד שיביא ב' שערות מאי איכא למימר? אמרי: לרבי ליכא תקנתא עד דיתיב דידיה ויתיב דאבוה - כלומר, לר' יוסי דאמר דאין האב מדירו אלא עד שמגיע לעונת נדרים, ניחא, דלא חייל עליה אלא נזירות אחת. אלא לרבי דאמר עד שיביא ב' שערות: כיון דאמר ״אהא בשביל אבא, אהא בשביל עצמי״, ושניהם יכולין להזיר, אמאי לא מיחייב בשתי נזירות? אמרי: לרבי לית ליה תקנתא עד דעביד דיליה ודאבוה. [לישנא אחרינא]: ״אלא לרבי דאמר כו'״ — הא ברשותיה דאבוה קאים כל זמן שלא הביא שתי שערות, וב' נזירות קביל עילויה, דאפילו רבי מודה דלכשהגיע לעונת נדרים מצי מזיר עצמו, ואפי' לא הביא שתי שערות, ואהדירו אבוה הוא דפליגי:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:1.english: This is the correct textual reading: “This works out well according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said: ‘Until he reaches the age of vows.’ However, according to Rebbi, who said: ‘Until he develops two hairs,’ what can be said? They say: According to Rebbi, he has no remedy until he sits [in naziriteship] for his [own vow] and sits for his father’s [vow]” - That is to say, according to Rabbi Yosei, who said that a father may vow on his [son's] behalf only until he reaches the age of vows, it works out well, as only one naziriteship takes effect upon him. However, according to Rebbi, who said [the father may vow for him] until he develops two hairs: since [the son] said, “I shall be [a nazirite] on account of Father; I shall be [a nazirite] on account of myself,” and both of them can impose naziriteship, why should he not be obligated in two naziriteships? They say: According to Rebbi, he has no remedy until he fulfills his [own naziriteship] and that of his father. [Another version]: “However, according to Rebbi, who said, etc.” — behold, he remains under his father’s authority as long as he has not developed two hairs, and he accepted two naziriteships upon himself! For even Rebbi concedes that once he reaches the age of vows, he can make himself a nazirite even if he has not developed two hairs, and it is [only] concerning his father’s vowing for him that they disagree.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:2.hebrew: ומשני אלא דאמר בלשון זה אהא בשביל אבא כו' - כלומר: אי אבא מצי להדירני — אהא נזיר בנדר אבא, ואם לאו — אהא נזיר בשביל עצמי. וכיון דאביו יכול להדירו, חד נזירות קביל לחודיה:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Rather, that he said with this wording: "I shall be [a nazirite] due to Father..." - That is to say: If Father is able to impose a vow upon me, I shall be a nazirite through Father's vow; and if not, I shall be a nazirite on my own account. And since his father is able to impose a vow upon him, he accepted only a single naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:3.hebrew: אי אייתי ב' שערות מעיקרא - קודם שהדירו אביו, קאים בנזירות דיליה ולא בנזירות דאביו, דיצא מרשות אביו:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:3.english: If he developed two hairs from the outset - Before his father imposed the vow upon him, he stands in his own naziriteship and not in his father's naziriteship, for he has left his father's authority.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:4.hebrew: ולבסוף - לאחר שבא לב"ד, קאים בנזירות דאבוה, דהא יש לאביו רשות בו. וכיון דמצי אביו להדירו, לא קביל עליה נזירות דיליה:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:4.english: And at the end - [That is, if he developed them] after he came before the court, he stands under his father’s naziriteship, for his father has authority over him. And since his father was able to make him a nazirite, he did not accept his own naziriteship upon himself.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:5.hebrew: ואי דאייתי במצעי - אחר שהדירו אביו, קודם שבא לב"ד, ולא ידעינן אי הני ב' שערות הוו ביה כשהדירו אביו, אי לא הוו ביה עד השתא — הא השתא, על כרחיך ימנה ב' נזירות מספיקא, דדילמא לא הוו ביה שתי שערות מעיקרא עד השתא, ונמצא נדור בשביל אביו; וכשבא לפני ב"ד ואמר "אהא בשביל עצמי", ויהא נזיר נמי בשביל עצמו, דהא הביא ב' שערות במיצעי. ואי "מייתי במיצעי מאי" — דודאי השתא אייתי ב' שערות, ונמצא דנדר אביו נדר, וכשבא לב"ד ואמר נמי "אהא בשביל עצמי", הוי נזיר בנדר דידיה, וימנה ב' נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:3:5.english: And if [the case is] that he developed [two hairs] in the middle - [Meaning,] after his father vowed [naziriteship] upon him, [but] before he came to the court, and we do not know whether these two hairs were on him when his father vowed upon him or whether they were not on him until now — behold now, perforce he must observe two [terms of] naziriteship out of doubt. For perhaps two hairs were not on him from the outset until now, and [thus] he turns out to be bound by vow on account of his father; and when he came before the court and said, "I will be [a nazirite] for myself," he should also be a nazirite for himself, since he developed two hairs in the middle. And if [the question,] "what if he develops [them] in the middle?" [means] that it is certain that he developed two hairs now, then it turns out that his father's vow is a [valid] vow; and when he came to the court and also said, "I will be [a nazirite] for myself," he is a nazirite through his own vow, and he must observe two [terms of] naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג במתניתין האיש מגלח על נזירות אביו כו' כיצד מי שהיה אביו נזיר והפריש מעות על נזירותו ומת ואמר הריני נזיר ע"מ שאגלח על מעות אבא אמר רבי יוסי הרי אלו יפלו לנדבה ואינו מגלח על נזירות אביו מי שהיה הוא ואביו נזירים והפריש מעות סתומין לנזירותו ומת זהו שמגלח כו': גמ' מ"ט - אין האשה מגלחת על נזירות אביה:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:5:1.english: This is the version in our Mishnah: “A man can shave by means of his father’s naziriteship, etc. How so? One whose father was a nazirite, and separated money for his naziriteship and died, and [the son] said: ‘I am hereby a nazirite on condition that I will shave by means of father’s money’ — Rabbi Yosei said: ‘These [coins] shall go to gift offerings, and he does not shave by means of his father’s naziriteship. One where he and his father were [both] nazirites, and [the father] separated unallocated money for his naziriteship and died, this is the one who shaves, etc.’” GEMARA: What is the reason? - [That is, why] a woman does not shave by means of her father’s naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:7:1.hebrew: הלכה היא בנזיר - שהבן מגלח, ואין לנו ללמוד הימנו אלא מה שמסורת הוא בידינו — בן, ולא בת:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:7:1.english: It is a halakha with regard to a nazirite - That the son shaves [on his father's naziriteship], and we can derive from it only that which is a tradition in our hands: a son, and not a daughter.

Rashi on Nazir 30a:7:2.hebrew: פשיטא - שהבן מגלח ולא הבת, דאין לבת במקום הבן כלום; והלכה למה לי:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:7:2.english: [It is] obvious - That the son shaves and not the daughter, for a daughter has nothing [of the inheritance] where there is a son; and why do I need a halakha?

Rashi on Nazir 30a:8:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא יורשין גמירי לה - שמגלחין על נזירות האב, ולא שנא בן, לא שנא בת במקום שאין בן:
Rashi on Nazir 30a:8:1.english: Lest you say that we learned [the tradition with regard to] heirs - That they may shave for the naziriteship of the father, and it makes no difference [whether it is] a son or a daughter in a place where there is no son.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:1:1.hebrew: ואמאי הא ברשותיה דאב קאים - [ואפי'] הוי גדול, דקס"ד "דגדול אני" היינו גדול לענין דנדרו נדר, דהיינו (לענין) משהגיע לעונת נדרים, עד שיביא ב' שערות מצי מדיר ליה; ותנא קמא אמר: [לידע אם הביא] ב' שערות. "אלא דאמר: אהא בשביל אבא, אהא בשביל עצמי" — כלומר, לא קאמר: "דאם קטן — שאין נדרו נדר, ואם גדול — שנדרו נדר", אלא: "אם קטן אני — שרשות אבי עלי, דהיינו עד הבאת שתי שערות". והאי דקאמר: "אם גדול" — י"א דלא גרסינן ליה, או שמא ר"ל: "ואם גדול — שהביא שתי שערות", וכרבי, דאמר דמדיר בנו עד הבאת שתי שערות:
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:1:1.english: "And why? After all, he remains under his father’s authority" - [Even if] he is an adult — for it entered our mind that "I am an adult" means an adult with regard to his vow being a [valid] vow, that is, (with regard to) from when he reaches the age of vows, [nevertheless] until he develops two hairs [his father] can vow for him; and the First Tanna said [that Rabban Gamliel examined him] to know if he had developed two hairs. "Rather, that he said: I shall be [a nazir] due to Father, I shall be due to myself" — that is to say, he did not say: "For if [I am] a minor, whose vow is not a vow, and if [I am] an adult, whose vow is a vow"; rather, "If I am a minor — that my father’s authority is over me, which is until the development of two hairs." And as for that which [the baraita] states: "If [I am] an adult" — some say that we do not have this in the text; or perhaps it means: "And if [I am] an adult — who has developed two hairs," and in accordance with Rabbi, who said that [a father] can vow for his son until the development of two hairs.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג: אי אייתי ב' שערות מעיקרא — קאי (ברשותיה) בנזירות דידיה, ואי בסוף — קאי בנזירות דאבוה; כי אייתי במיצעי מאי? הניחא לרבי יוסי בר' יהודה דאמר לעונת נדרים, אלא לרבי מאי? ליכא תקנתא עד דיתיב דיליה ויתיב דאבוה - וכן הגיהו בפי' קדמונים, וה"פ רבינו חננאל: "אי אייתי מעיקרא" — כלומר, אם בדקוהו באותה שעה שבא לפני רבן גמליאל, ביום שהדירו אביו, ומצאו לו ב' שערות, קאי בנדרים דידיה, ונדרו בשביל עצמו. "ואי לבסוף" — כלומר, עכשיו שלא נבדק באותו היום, אם לא יביא שתי שערות עד לבסוף ל' יום, דאישתכח דודאי אלו ל' יום היו בשביל נדר אביו. "אלא אייתי במיצעי" — כלומר, נראו בו סימנים תוך ל', היאך יצא ידי נזירות באותן שלשים יום? שהרי נזירות אביו מתבטל (עד) אחר הבאת סימנים, ואיך יביא קרבנותיו לסוף שלשים יום שהדירו אביו? וליכא למימר דדעתו היה שאפי' יביא סימנים שלא יפסיק נזירות אביו — מכל מקום אינו ראוי להביא קרבן בשביל נזירות אביו לבד, וגם בשביל עצמו, כיון שלא פירש. וא"ת: ואמאי לא פריך הכי [למתניתין], דהיאך מדיר בנו בנזיר, כי מייתי במיצעי מאי? וי"ל: דמתני' איכא לאוקמי בעודו בשנת י"ב, דאף אם מביא — הם שומא. אבל אהא קא קשיא ליה, דקאי ליה אחר שנת י"ג שנה, מדקמייתי לת"ק למיבדקיה אם הביא אם לאו, דקודם לכן שומא אינון. אי נמי, יש לפרש: דאמתני' ליכא למיפרך, דודאי בדקינן במלאת ימי נזירותו, ואי מספקינן אי אייתי סימנים במיצעי — לא (נבדיקיה). אבל אהא קשיא ליה, דקאמר "דלא תצטער לבדקני, דבלא בדיקה תיקן הכל בתנאו דאם קטן אני", כאילו [לא] היה שם בדיקה צורך; ולכך פריך, דהא ודאי אי אייתי במיצעי — אינו מתוקן כלל:
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:2:1.english: This is the reading: "If he had developed two hairs from the outset, he stands (under his own authority) in his own naziriteship; and if at the end, he stands in his father's naziriteship. If he developed [them] in the middle, what [is the law]? This works out well according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said: Until he reaches the age of vows; but according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], what [can be said]? There is no remedy until he sits [for the term of] his own and sits [for the term of] his father" - And so they emended in the commentary of early authorities, and this is how Rabbeinu Chananel explained it: "If he had developed [two hairs] from the outset" — that is to say: If they had examined him at that time when he came before Rabban Gamliel, on the day his father vowed for him, and they found two hairs on him, he stands in his own vows, and his vow was on his own behalf. "And if at the end" — that is to say: Now that he was not examined on that day, if he does not develop two hairs until the end of thirty days, so that it is found that these thirty days were certainly on account of his father's vow. "Rather, if he developed [them] in the middle" — that is to say: [If] signs [of puberty] appeared on him within thirty [days], how could he fulfill the obligation of naziriteship during those thirty days? For his father's naziriteship is cancelled (until) after the appearance of signs [of puberty], and how could he bring his offerings at the end of the thirty days that his father vowed for him? And one cannot say that his intention was that even if he develops signs [of puberty], his father's naziriteship should not cease — nevertheless, he is not fit to bring an offering for his father's naziriteship alone, nor for himself, since he did not specify [such a condition]. And if you say: And why didn't [the Gemara] ask this against [the Mishnah]: How can [a father] vow for his son to be a nazirite — if he develops [two hairs] in the middle, what [is the law]? And one can say [in answer]: The Mishnah can be established [as speaking of] when he is still in his twelfth year, for even if he develops [hairs], they are [merely] a mole. But regarding this [baraita] it was difficult to [the Gemara], because [the boy here] is already after thirteen years of age, since according to the first Tanna they brought him to examine him whether he had developed [two hairs] or whether he had not, for prior to that [age] they are [merely] a mole. Alternatively, it can be explained: Against the Mishnah one cannot raise an objection, for certainly we examine [the boy] at the completion of the days of his naziriteship, and if we are in doubt whether he developed signs [of puberty] in the middle, we do not (examine him). But regarding this [baraita] it was difficult to [the Gemara], where [the boy] said, 'Do not go to the trouble of examining me, for without an examination everything was rectified by his condition of: If I am a minor...' — as if there were [no] need for an examination there! And therefore [the Gemara] objects that, certainly, if he developed [signs of puberty] in the middle, it is not rectified at all.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:3:1.hebrew: הניחא לר' יוסי בר' יהודה דאמר עד שיגיע לעונת נדרים - והוא עומד בשנת י"ב, ליכא למיחש, דהוי שומא. וא"ת: ניחוש שמא בא לעונת נדרים במיצעי, וא"כ איך יצא בנזירות אביו לבד ל' יום? ופר"ת, דעונת נדרים אינה סותרת: דנהי דהאב אינו יכול להדירו מכאן ואילך, מכל מקום היכא דהדירו קודם לכן — משום עונת נדרים לא פקע, כיון דלא הוי כ"א דרבנן; אבל שערות, דאיש דאורייתא — פקע דאביו. וא"כ, ניחוש לשערות במיצעי? י"ל דמיירי תחילת י"ג, דאכתי אי הוה ליה במיצעי — ה"ל שומא בעלמא. ואף אם בא לכלל עונת נדרים באמצע נזירות, אין להקפיד, לפירוש רבינו תם דעונת נדרים אינה סותרת; דנהי נמי דאין מדירו (אלא) כשהגיע לעונת נדרים — אכתי קאי בקטנותו, וכל כמה דלא הדר ביה הוה בנדר אביו, וגם שמא לא יוכל למחות באמצע. אלא לרבי דאמר: "עד שיביא שתי שערות", והביאו לבדקו בשנת י"ד לידע — אם הביא במיצעי, מאי:
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:3:1.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said: "Until he reaches the age of vows" - And [since] he is standing in his twelfth year, there is no concern [of pubic hairs], as [any hair grown at this age] is a mere mole. And if you say: Let us be concerned lest he entered the age of vows in the middle [of the thirty days], and if so, how did he fulfill [his obligation] through his father's naziriteship alone for thirty days? Rabbeinu Tam explained that [reaching] the age of vows does not cancel [a prior naziriteship]. For although the father cannot vow on his behalf from this point forward, nevertheless, where he vowed on his behalf prior to this, it does not lapse on account of the age of vows, since it is only rabbinic. However, [bringing two] hairs, which makes him an adult by Torah law, cancels [the authority of] his father. And if so, let us be concerned about hairs in the middle? One can say that [Rabbi Yosei] is dealing with the beginning of the thirteenth year, for still, if he were to develop [hairs] in the middle, they would be a mere mole. And even if he reached the status of the age of vows in the middle of the naziriteship, there is no concern according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam that [reaching] the age of vows does not cancel [the vow]. For even granted that [a father] does not vow on his behalf once he has reached the age of vows, he still remains in his minority, and as long as he has not retracted it, he remains under his father's vow; and also, perhaps he cannot protest in the middle. Rather, [the Gemara's question is] according to Rabbi, who said: "Until he brings two hairs," and they brought him to examine him in his fourteenth year, to know: If he brought [hairs] in the middle, what [is the halakha]?

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:4:1.hebrew: לרבי ליכא תקנתא עד דיתיב דידיה - פירוש: שצריך שימתין ר' חנינא (ל') יום אחר שהדירו אביו, דאז ממה נפשך איכא [שלשים]: או לפני הבאת סימנים, או אחר הבאת סימנים, ועלתה לו נזירות אביו:
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:4:1.english: According to Rabbi, there is no remedy until he observes his own - Explanation: Rabbi Chanina must wait [thirty] days after [the period] his father vowed for him, for then, either way, there are [thirty days] either before the appearance of signs [of puberty] or after the appearance of signs, and his father's naziriteship counts for him.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:5:1.hebrew: האיש מגלח על נזירות אביו ואין אשה מגלחת - כיצד? מי שהיה הוא ואביו נזירים, והפריש אביו מעות לנזירותו ומת — ר' יוסי אומר: הרי אלו יפלו לנדבה. ואיזהו שמגלח על נזירות אביו? הרי שהיה אביו נזיר, והיו לו מעות סתומין ומת, ואמר: ״הריני נזיר ע"מ שאגלח על מעות אבא״ — זהו שמגלח על נזירות אביו — ה"ג בפירוש קדמונים ובפירוש רבינו ברוך. ובהרבה ספרים היא: דהוא ואביו נזיר מגלח על מעות אביו, ואם בחיי אביו אינו מגלח:
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:5:1.english: "A man can shave by his father’s naziriteship, but a woman cannot shave" - "How so? [If] he and his father were nazirites, and his father separated money for his naziriteship and died, Rabbi Yosei says: These [coins] shall go for gift offerings. And who is the one who shaves by his father’s naziriteship? If his father was a nazirite and had unallocated money and died, and he said: 'I am hereby a nazirite on the condition that I shave by father's money' — this is the one who shaves by his father's naziriteship" — this is the reading in the commentary of the early authorities [Peirush Kadmonim] and in the commentary of Rabbeinu Baruch. And in many books it is [the reading]: that [when] he and his father [were] nazirites he shaves by his father’s money, and if in his father’s lifetime, he does not shave.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:7:1.english: "What is the reason" - [Why] a woman does not shave using her father's money.

Tosafot on Nazir 30a:7:2.hebrew: פשיטא - בלא הלכה ידעינן דאין בת מגלחת, ולמאי הוצרך מילתא דר' יוחנן? וא"כ, הא דקאמר הש"ס "מ"ט", מאי קושיא, דהכא פשוט לן דבן ולא בת? וצ"ל דר' יוחנן גופיה אמרה, כי הך דבפ' אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כא.): "וכמה? אמר ר' יצחק: קב בארבע אמות". (וע"ע תוספות פסחים לג: ד"ה תתן וכו' ומה שנרשם שם):
Tosafot on Nazir 30a:7:2.english: "It is obvious" - Even without a halakha, we know that a daughter does not shave [using her father's animals]. For what, then, was Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement needed? And if so, that which the Gemara asks: "What is the reason?" — what was its difficulty, since here it is obvious to us that a son [inherits] and not a daughter? And one must say that Rabbi Yoḥanan himself said it, like that [case] in the chapter [entitled] Elu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 21a): "And how much? Rabbi Yitzḥak said: A kav in four cubits." (And see further Tosafot, Pesachim 33b, s.v. Titen, etc., and what is noted there.)
